topics.label: Course conclusion and lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and outline the learning objectives for the final lecture on cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer treatment, focusing on their mechanisms of action, clinical utility, and the limiting effects of non-specific toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover therapeutic approaches designed to exploit specific biological weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale of targeting oncogene-addicted kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and detail the biological mechanisms underlying acquired resistance, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how engineered monoclonal antibodies and conjugated cytotoxic agents are targeted against specific cell-surface proteins to destroy tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance, checkpoint inhibitors, and engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the evidence for host immune surveillance and evaluate strategies to harness the immune response, including immune checkpoint blockade, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the overarching challenges facing modern oncology, including tumor heterogeneity, genomic stratification, historical survival patterns, and the clinical dilemmas surrounding therapy selection.
